We further assume that the unimodal structure is preserved

conditions: rewards from the parametrized family V

source.label: th:graves_lai
source.quote: Let $\pi\in \Pi$ be a uniformly good algorithm, and assume that $\nu_k = \nu(\theta_k) \in {\cal V}$ for all $k$. Then for any $\theta\in \Theta_G$, \lim \inf_{T \to +\infty} \frac{R^{\pi}(T)}{ \log(T)}  \geq c(\theta) = \sum_{(k,k^*) \in E} \frac{ \mu^{\star} - \mu_k}{I_{\min}(\theta_k, \theta^{\star})}.

results.notes: Derived via Graves-Lai; c(theta) only involves neighbours of the optimal arm. Regret defined through expected pull counts (pseudo-regret).

bound.regime: suboptimal arm k adjacent to k* in G

symbols.mu_k: mean of the suboptimal arm k

tuning: c > 0 constant in the index F

source.label: th:kluucb_finite
source.quote: The number of times suboptimal arm $k$ is selected under OSUB satisfies: for all $\epsilon>0$ and all $T\ge 3$, \EE[ t_k(T) ] \leq (1 + \epsilon) \frac{ \log(T) + c \log(\log(T))}{ I(\mu_k,\mu^*)} + C_1 \log \log (T) + \frac{C_2}{T^{\beta(\epsilon)}} if (k,k^\star) \in E, \frac{C_3}{\Delta^2} otherwise

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls E[t_k(T)], not regret. I is Bernoulli KL. Note the proof only shows O(log log T) for non-neighbours, despite the C_3/Delta^2 statement.

bound.regime: suboptimal arm k not adjacent to k* in G

symbols.Delta_G: min over arms k of (mu of best neighbour of k minus mu_k)

tuning: c > 0 constant in the index F
results.notes: Expected pull count of non-neighbour suboptimal arms. The appendix proof establishes O(log log T) for E[l_k(T)], which seems inconsistent with a T-independent constant; recorded as stated.

symbols.C_lin: c(theta) = sum over neighbours k of k* of (mu_star - mu_k)/kl(mu_k, mu_star)

source.quote: Assume that rewards distributions are Bernoulli (i.e for any $k$, $\nu_k \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\theta_k)$), and that $\theta\in \Theta_G$. Then the regret achieved under $\pi$=OSUB satisfies: $\lim \sup_{T \to +\infty} R^{\pi}(T) / \log(T) \leq c(\theta).$

results.notes: Matches the lower bound of Theorem 4.1 for Bernoulli rewards.

bound.expression: H_DT*(1 + Delta_sep) + T*C_1*K*log(tau)/(tau*(Delta_sep - 4*tau*sigma_lip)**2) + T*gamma_deg*(1 + g_0**(-1/2))*(log(tau) + c_alg*log(log(tau)) + C_2)/(2*tau*(Delta_sep - 2*tau*sigma_lip)**2)

symbols.H_DT: H(Delta,T): number of (round, edge) pairs with |mu_k(n)-mu_k'(n)| < Delta
symbols.Delta_sep: free separation threshold Delta in (2 tau sigma, Delta_0)
symbols.sigma_lip: Lipschitz drift speed of the means

conditions: mu(n) unimodal w.r.t. G for all n

source.label: th:nonstat
source.quote: Let $\Delta$: $2\tau\sigma < \Delta < \Delta_0$. Assume that for any $n\ge 1$, $\mu(n)\in {\cal U}_G$ and $\mu^\star(n)\in [a,1-a]$ for some $a>0$. Further suppose that $\mu_k(\cdot)$ is $\sigma$-Lipschitz for any $k$. The regret per unit time under $\pi=$SW-OSUB with a sliding window of size $\tau+1$ satisfies: if $a>\sigma\tau$, then for any $T\ge 1$, ...

results.notes: Stated as regret per unit time; multiplied by T. Regret is against per-round best arm (dynamic regret). Second term would require Delta > 4 tau sigma to be meaningful.

symbols.sigma_lip: Lipschitz drift speed of the means
symbols.j_sigma: j(sigma), a function with j(sigma) -> 0 as sigma -> 0+

conditions: Assumption 1: limsup H(Delta,T)/T <= Phi(K) Delta for Delta < Delta_0

source.quote: Set $\tau = \sigma^{-3/4} \log(1/\sigma) / 8 $. The regret per unit of time of $\pi=$SW-OSUB with window size $\tau+1$ satisfies: $\lim \sup_{T\to\infty} \frac{R^{\pi}(T)}{T}  \leq C \Phi(K) \sigma^{\frac{1}{4}} \log \Lp \frac{1}{\sigma} \Rp ( 1 + K j(\sigma) )$

results.notes: Per-unit-time bound multiplied by T. Window tuned using sigma, so the algorithm needs the drift speed (not in vocabulary). Assumption 1 is used implicitly.

source.quote: Let $\Delta$: $2\tau\sigma < \Delta < \Delta_0$. Assume that for any $n\ge 1$, $\mu^\star(n)\in [a,1-a]$ for some $a>0$. Further suppose that $\mu_k(\cdot)$ is $\sigma$-Lipschitz for any $k$. The regret per unit time under $\pi=$SW-KL-UCB with a sliding window of size $\tau$ satisfies: if $a>\sigma\tau$, then for any $T\ge 1$, ...

results.notes: SW-KL-UCB does not use unimodality; the setting s4's unimodality is not needed. Per-unit-time bound multiplied by T.

conditions: Assumption 2: C_1|x-y|^alpha <= |mu(x)-mu(y)| near x*, and |mu(x*)-mu(x)| <= C_2 delta^alpha for |x-x*| <= delta <= delta_0

source.label: th:unimodal_cont
source.quote: Consider a unimodal bandit on $[0,1]$ with rewards in $[0,1]$ and satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:22}. Set $\delta= (\log(T)/\sqrt{T} )^{1/\alpha}$. The regret under UCB($\delta$) satisfies: \lim \sup_{T\to\infty} {R^{\pi}(T) \over \sqrt{T} \log(T)} \leq C_2 3^{\alpha} + 16 /C_1.

results.notes: Discretization uses T and alpha. Instance constants C_1, C_2, alpha enter the bound; classified worst_case over the class satisfying Assumption 2.
